title: LLM Inference Attack Simulation and Pen-Test Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the safe, repeatable process for performing adversarial attack simulations and penetration tests against Redwood Inference LLM serving stacks. The goal is to validate runtime resilience, SLO preservation, telemetry fidelity, and safety controls under adversarial inputs and attack patterns (rate-floods, prompt injection, token-leak scenarios, KV‑cache exhaustion, and malformed stream frames).

Intended audience:
- Platform operators and SREs running LLM fleets
- Runtime engineers and inference runtime owners
- Security team members coordinating pen tests
- Solutions and customer-facing engineers preparing sensitive environments

Scope and exclusions:
- Includes hosted and dedicated inference endpoints and edge proxies (ingress layer).
- Includes controlled tests against private deployments only with explicit customer authorization (see Safety & Compliance Preconditions).
- Excludes adversarial model training or data poisoning (tracked separately by Applied ML).

High-level goals:
- Exercise graceful degradation and fallback policies without violating SLAs for safety-critical tenants.
- Verify alerting and dashboards for attack surface indicators (token spikes, KV cache churn, anomalous response entropy).
- Confirm enforcement of tenancy and quota controls, and validate automatic tenant throttling/eviction logic.
- Produce a prioritized remediation list and measurable regression tests for CI.

Roles & ownership:
- Test Lead (owner): platform QA lead or SRE engineer (primary runbook executor).
- Incident Liaison: oncall engineer for the region being tested.
- Security Reviewer: security engineer responsible for scope and blast radius approval.
- Runtime Owner: owner of the target model-serving service.
- Customer Contact (if testing private/dedicated): named customer security/ops rep with written permission.

Safety & Compliance Preconditions (MUST):
1) Written authorization for any non‑test tenants impacted.
2) Approval from Security Reviewer and Runtime Owner recorded in the test ticket.
3) Simulation run window scheduled during low-traffic maintenance window unless explicitly waived.
4) Canary-only experiments for production routes limited to 1% traffic forwarders and using synthetic tokens.
5) Abort criteria defined and watchers assigned (automated abort threshold and human oncall).

Abort criteria (examples):
- P99 latency > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes for more than 10% of production requests.
- Token cost per minute spike > 3x baseline and sustained for 2 minutes.
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase above baseline for 5 minutes.
- Any customer-reported degradation flagged by customer contact.

Attack scenario catalog (table):
| id | name | description | primary metric | safe blast mitigation |
|----|------|-------------|----------------|----------------------|
| A1 | Rate-flood (ingress) | High-QPS synthetic flood against public model endpoint | p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate | throttling, global ingress limiters |
| A2 | Token-ecstasy | Repeated long-context prompts to inflate token generation | token/sec, token-cost | token caps, per-tenant rate limits |
| A3 | Prompt-injection | Inputs crafted to exfiltrate system prompts or induce unsafe outputs | alert on high-entropy responses, data-leak detectors | content filters, model-variant fallback |
| A4 | KV-cache-exhaust | Many unique prefixes producing heavy KV growth leading to memory pressure | cache-miss rate, evictions/sec, OOM counts | eviction policies, pre-warming, circuit breaker |
| A5 | Malformed-stream-frames | Fragmented/invalid streaming frames to test parser resilience | stream-errors, connection resets | ingress validation, connection rate limiting |

Metrics & dashboards to verify (minimum):
- Latency slices: p50/p95/p99 per route and per-model variant (Prometheus series: inference_latency_seconds_bucket{route,model_variant}).
- Token economics: tokens_generated_total by tenant and route.
- KV cache health: kv_cache_entries{shard}, kv_evictions_total, kv_miss_rate.
- Error taxonomy: 4xx vs 5xx by route and upstream cause.
- Response entropy / content_classifier_score: signal for possible data leak or prompt-injection success.
- Ingress connection churn: tcp_connections_open, stream_frame_parsing_errors.

Suggested dashboard panels (PromQL examples):
- P99 latency (route="/v1/generate"):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))

- Tokens/sec by tenant (top 10):
  topk(10, sum(rate(tokens_generated_total[1m])) by (tenant))

- KV eviction spikes:
  increase(kv_evictions_total[5m]) > 0

- Prompt-injection alert baseline:
  sum(rate(content_classifier_high_risk_total[5m])) by (route) > 5

Pre-simulation checklist (operator must complete):
- [ ] Ticket created with scope, approvals, and rollback plan (link ticket ID).
- [ ] Watchers assigned and contactable via Slack + phone.
- [ ] Synthetic tenants and API keys prepared; no real customer keys used.
- [ ] Dashboard pinned and notification rules set (PagerDuty + email).
- [ ] Automated abort thresholds configured in the test harness.
- [ ] Backout playbook staged and dry-runned in staging environment.

Simulation runbook (ordered steps):
1. Initiate pre-checks: verify baseline telemetry for last 24 hours and save snapshots.
2. Start a small-scale smoke run (10% of planned intensity) for 3 minutes; validate metrics and proceed only on green.
3. Gradually ramp traffic as per the ramp profile for the scenario (example ramp schedule below).
4. Monitor live dashboards and alert channels for abort conditions.
5. At midpoint, trigger a model-variant fallback to verify graceful fallback (if applicable).
6. Run post-failure recovery steps: reduce traffic, exercise eviction/cooldown, and confirm system returns to baseline.
7. End simulation and collect artifacts: traces, flamegraphs, Prometheus scrapes, ingress logs, and the test harness logs.

Example ramp profile (A1 rate-flood):
- 0-2m: 5% intensity
- 2-6m: 20% intensity
- 6-12m: 60% intensity
- 12-18m: 100% intensity for no more than 6 minutes
- 18-22m: step down to 10% and stabilize

Test harness example (curl + k6 snippet):
- k6 pseudo-YAML to simulate token-heavy generation (illustrative):
  ```yaml
  scenarios:
    token_spike:
      executor: constant-vus
      vus: 50
      duration: 10m
      exec: generate
  ```
- Simple curl example to exercise streaming parser (use synthetic key):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer SYNTH_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-6B","prompt":"\"repeat:a:\" * 2000","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate

Post-simulation analysis and evidence collection:
- Required artifacts:
  - Saved Prometheus snapshot (raw series) covering 30m pre/30m during/30m post test.
  - Representative traces from the tracer (span ids).
  - Ingress & backend logs (redact customer identifiers).
  - Test harness logs and seed files used to generate inputs.
- Analysis checklist:
  - Identify top 5 root causes (latency, OOM, eviction, parsing errors, auth failures).
  - Map each root cause to a remediation and assign an owner with a target date.
  - Create CI test that reproduces the regression in the staging harness where possible.

Remediation prioritization matrix (example):
- Priority P0: crash, data-exfiltration vector, or production OOM (fix immediate, pager).
- Priority P1: SLO regressions > defined thresholds or noisy operator toil.
- Priority P2: Observability gaps and hard-to-reproduce edge cases.

Communication & change control:
- Produce a concise summary email/slack for engineering leadership within 24 hours including: scenario, impact, artifacts, and P0/P1 actions.
- Post remediation, require a follow-up simulation to verify fixes (regression window 7–14 days).

Template: incident ticket summary (copy into Jira/Confluence):
- Title: [Sim] A1 Rate-Flood — region-us-west-2 — <date>
- Scope: routes, tenants, model-variants
- Blast radius: synthetic tenants only / % of production traffic
- Abort conditions triggered: yes/no (timestamp)
- Artifacts: link to prometheus snapshot, traces, harness logs
- Findings: bullet list of 1–5 items
- Actions: owner + due date

Operationalization and CI integration:
- Add each validated simulation profile to the platform CI nightly canary suite (staging only) with reduced intensity.
- For each remediation, add unit/integration checks that assert non‑regression for the metric most impacted (e.g., p99 latency < baseline * 1.3).

Appendix: quick reference commands and queries
- Capture 1 minute p99 across region:
  curl -s "https://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99,sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))" | jq .

- Simple eviction inspector (go tool pseudo):
  ./bin/kv-inspect --shard=3 --window=5m --top=20

- Safety reminder: never run tests against customer-managed private deployments without explicit, written customer approval recorded in the ticket.
